{"summary": "Passive OSINT assessment of python.org focused on e-mail security posture (SPF, DMARC, DKIM, alignment) and subdomain/certificate hygiene.

1. SPF POSTURE
- Record present: yes, single TXT SPF record published on python.org
- Mechanism: v=spf1 mx ip4:188.166.95.178/32 ip6:2a03:b0c0:2:d0::71:1 include:stspg-customer.com include:_spf.google.com include:mailgun.org ~all
- Qualifier: softfail (~all) — unlisted senders are marked suspicious but not rejected
- Sending sources: own MX (mail.python.org), one hardcoded IPv4/IPv6 host, Statuspage (stspg-customer.com), Google Workspace (_spf.google.com), Mailgun
- Lookup count: 4 includes + mx + ip4 + ip6 = 7 DNS-lookup-consuming terms, within the RFC 7208 limit of 10 but with limited headroom
- Observations: the record is broad (three third-party includes) and the hardcoded IPs are not documented; softfail weakens spoofing protection compared to -all

2. DMARC POSTURE
- Record present: yes on python.org
- Policy: p=none (monitoring only, no enforcement)
- Subdomain policy: no sp= observed in the collected data
- Alignment: not observable from the collected data (rua/ruf/pct/aspf/adkim not returned)
- Consequence: with p=none, even a failing SPF/DKIM result does not cause rejection or quarantine; spoofed mail claiming to be from python.org can still be delivered
- Subdomain coverage: lists.es.python.org also publishes DMARC with p=none, i.e. the same non-enforcing posture

3. DKIM HINTS
- Selector found: "google" (consistent with Google Workspace as a sending source)
- Not found: no selectors detected for Mailgun or Statuspage in the probed common selector set
- Caveat: only common selectors were probed; absence is not proof of missing DKIM
- Alignment risk: with p=none, DKIM alignment is not enforced, so a missing or misaligned Mailgun/Statuspage signature would go unnoticed

4. SENDING SUBDOMAINS AND DELEGATION
- mail.python.org: primary MX (priority 50); no SPF, no DMARC, no DKIM selectors observed on the host itself — it relies on the organizational-domain policy
- lists.es.python.org: delegated to a third-party operator (MX smtp.jcea.es, NS dns.jcea.es/dns2.jcea.es); own SPF with hardfail (-all) but DMARC p=none
- Other mail-adjacent hosts in CT logs: smtp-like naming not observed, but mail-adjacent services include discuss.python.org, lists.es.python.org, cla.python.org, membership.uk.python.org, login.python.org
- Orphaned-sending risk: several community/regional subdomains (es., uk., pl., id., africa.) are operated by separate volunteers/entities; no evidence in the collected data that they inherit an enforcing policy
- No explicit smtp.* or mailer.* subdomains were found in the CT enumeration

5. CERTIFICATE TRANSPARENCY / HYGIENE
- Subdomains enumerated: 76 (crt.sh), not truncated
- Notable exposure: staging and preview environments visible in CT logs — staging.python.org, blog-stage.python.org, donate-preview.python.org, ghsponsors-stage.python.org, legacy.python.org, testpypi.python.org
- Legacy/obsolete services still resolvable in CT: svn.python.org, hg.python.org, hg.es.python.org, www.hg.es.python.org, packages.python.org, cheeseshop.python.org
- Wildcard/aggregation: no wildcard certificate evidence in the returned data; the large number of distinct hostnames suggests per-host issuance
- Hygiene note: staging/preview hostnames in CT logs are a common source of unintended mail-sending or credential-exposure paths, though no direct mail-sending evidence was collected

6. VERIFICATION AND THIRD-PARTY RECORDS
- 13 TXT records on the apex, including multiple google-site-verification tokens (4), MS= (Microsoft), openai-domain-verification, anthropic-domain-verification, twilio-domain-verification, status-page-domain-verification, _globalsign-domain-verification, libera-1298aas, and one opaque hash
- Assessment: these are benign ownership proofs, but they reveal a broad third-party service footprint and are a minor hygiene concern (stale tokens should be pruned)

7. LIMITATIONS
- Data comes from a single passive DNS resolver and crt.sh; DMARC rua/ruf/pct/aspf/adkim tags, full DKIM selector inventory and actual message authentication results were not observable

data.summary:
Corrected passive-reconnaissance synthesis for python.org, limited to the collected DNS and crt.sh data.

1. SPF POSTURE
- Apex record: v=spf1 mx ip4:188.166.95.178/32 ip6:2a03:b0c0:2:d0::71:1 include:stspg-customer.com include:_spf.google.com include:mailgun.org ~all
- Lookup-consuming terms: 6 (3 includes + mx + ip4 + ip6), leaving roughly 4 of the 10 permitted DNS lookups as headroom
- Qualifier: ~all (softfail), not -all; unlisted senders are marked but not rejected
- Third-party senders authorized: Statuspage (stspg-customer.com), Google Workspace (_spf.google.com), Mailgun (mailgun.org)
- Explicit IPs: one IPv4 (/32) and one IPv6 host address authorized directly

2. DMARC POSTURE
- Apex DMARC: present; the tool reports dmarc_policy = none (no record text, rua/ruf, pct, aspf or adkim values were returned)
- Effect: no enforcement; receivers are given no instruction to quarantine or reject failing mail
- Alignment: not observable from the collected data
- Subdomain policy: not returned

3. DKIM
- Selector found: "google" on the apex (common-selector probe only)
- Caveat: absence of other selectors is not proof that DKIM is missing; Mailgun and Statuspage selectors were not probed
- Alignment with SPF/DMARC: not assessable from the collected data

4. MAIL ROUTING AND SUBDOMAINS
- Apex MX: single record "50 mail.python.org" (priority 50) on python.org
- mail.python.org: the lookup of this host itself returned no MX, NS or TXT records; it is only known as the apex MX target
- lists.es.python.org: separate MX (10 smtp.jcea.es) and separate NS (dns.jcea.es, dns2.jcea.es); publishes its own SPF "v=spf1 include:jcea.es -all" (hardfail); the tool reports dmarc_policy = none for this host
- CT enumeration: 76 hostnames returned by crt.sh, not truncated; no smtp.* or mailer.* hostnames appear in that list (a weak negative, limited to CT coverage)
- Hostnames present in CT logs that suggest legacy or non-current services: svn.python.org, hg.python.org, packages.python.org, cheeseshop.python.org, buildbot.python.org, speed.python.org, legacy.python.org, pypi.python.org, testpypi.python.org, clabot.python.org, memory.python.org, console.python.org, analytics.python.org, staging.python.org, blog-stage.python.org, donate-preview.python.org, ghsponsors-stage.python.org
- No DNS resolution was performed on these hosts; only their presence in CT logs is established
- Certificate data: none collected; only a crt.sh hostname list, so no statement on wildcard usage or issuance pattern is possible

5. APEX TXT RECORD HYGIENE
- Total: 13 TXT records on python.org
- Verification tokens: 4 google-site-verification, 1 MS= (Microsoft), 1 openai-domain-verification, 1 anthropic-domain-verification, 1 twilio-domain-verification, 1 status-page-domain-verification, 1 _globalsign-domain-verification
- Other: "libera-1298aas" and one opaque hash (888acb5757da46ad83b7e341ec544c64)
- Observation: a large number of third-party verification tokens increases the chance of stale entries that should be reviewed periodically

6. DATA LIMITATIONS
- Sources used: system DNS resolver and crt.sh only
- Not collected: DMARC record text, DKIM selectors beyond common probes, certificate details, DNS resolution of enumerated hosts
- Conclusions are therefore bounded to what these two sources returned
data.risk_justification: SPF is published and reasonably scoped (6 of 10 lookups used, softfail ~all), and a DKIM selector ("google") is visible, but DMARC is reported at p=none, meaning no enforcement against spoofing of python.org. For a high-profile domain, the absence of a quarantine/reject policy leaves display-name and direct-domain spoofing viable. The risk is not rated high because SPF exists, a DKIM selector is present, and the apex has a single MX; it is not rated low because DMARC enforcement is absent and the DMARC record details (alignment, reporting, pct) could not be verified. The separate lists.es.python.org host also reports p=none, and legacy hostnames remain present in CT logs, but no resolution or certificate data was collected to assess them further.
recommendations: Move the apex DMARC policy from p=none to p=quarantine and then p=reject, using a staged rollout with pct to monitor impact.
Retrieve and review the full DMARC record text (rua/ruf, pct, aspf, adkim, sp) to confirm reporting and alignment settings, which were not returned by the collection tools.
Verify DKIM signing for all three authorized senders (Google, Mailgun, Statuspage) by probing their specific selectors, not only the common 'google' selector.
Consider tightening SPF from ~all to -all once all legitimate senders are confirmed, keeping the lookup count at 6 of 10.
Review the 13 apex TXT records and remove stale third-party verification tokens that are no longer needed.

Confirm whether legacy hostnames seen in CT logs (svn, hg, packages, cheeseshop, buildbot, legacy, pypi) are still active and, if so, whether they are covered by the domain's mail policy; no resolution was performed, so this requires follow-up.
Assess whether lists.es.python.org, which publishes its own SPF and reports p=none, should adopt an enforcing DMARC policy consistent with the parent domain.

Passive OSINT assessment of python.org focused on e-mail security posture (SPF, DMARC, DKIM, alignment) and subdomain/certificate hygiene.

1. SPF POSTURE
- Record present: yes, single TXT SPF record published on python.org
- Mechanism: v=spf1 mx ip4:188.166.95.178/32 ip6:2a03:b0c0:2:d0::71:1 include:stspg-customer.com include:_spf.google.com include:mailgun.org ~all
- Qualifier: softfail (~all) — unlisted senders are marked suspicious but not rejected
- Sending sources: own MX (mail.python.org), one hardcoded IPv4/IPv6 host, Statuspage (stspg-customer.com), Google Workspace (_spf.google.com), Mailgun
- Lookup count: 4 includes + mx + ip4 + ip6 = 7 DNS-lookup-consuming terms, within the RFC 7208 limit of 10 but with limited headroom
- Observations: the record is broad (three third-party includes) and the hardcoded IPs are not documented; softfail weakens spoofing protection compared to -all

2. DMARC POSTURE
- Record present: yes on python.org
- Policy: p=none (monitoring only, no enforcement)
- Subdomain policy: no sp= observed in the collected data
- Alignment: not observable from the collected data (rua/ruf/pct/aspf/adkim not returned)
- Consequence: with p=none, even a failing SPF/DKIM result does not cause rejection or quarantine; spoofed mail claiming to be from python.org can still be delivered
- Subdomain coverage: lists.es.python.org also publishes DMARC with p=none, i.e. the same non-enforcing posture

3. DKIM HINTS
- Selector found: "google" (consistent with Google Workspace as a sending source)
- Not found: no selectors detected for Mailgun or Statuspage in the probed common selector set
- Caveat: only common selectors were probed; absence is not proof of missing DKIM
- Alignment risk: with p=none, DKIM alignment is not enforced, so a missing or misaligned Mailgun/Statuspage signature would go unnoticed

4. SENDING SUBDOMAINS AND DELEGATION
- mail.python.org: primary MX (priority 50); no SPF, no DMARC, no DKIM selectors observed on the host itself — it relies on the organizational-domain policy
